thread:
Sam: Heads-up — seeing weird flapping on eu-west-gpu when HPA scales pods based on external queue-depth metric and CA tries to add preemptible nodes. Pods get scheduled then evicted in a loop. Anyone else?
Priya: Noted. Is this the new inference-batch queue metric via external-metrics-adapter?
Sam: Yes, external metric from prometheus-rule -> adapter. HPA target is queue_depth per pod. When Q spikes to ~300 it scales to 30 replicas, CA requests 4 new gpu-preemptible nodes, nodes come up but pods get evicted with "Insufficient ephemeral-storage" then reschedule -> HPA sees lower per-pod qps -> scales down -> CA deletes nodes -> backlog still high -> repeat.
Marco: Interesting. Logs from kube-scheduler or kubelet? Could be kubelet disk pressure on node images for gpu drivers?
Sam: Kubelet reports ImagePullBackOff for the runtime init container sometimes; also eviction threshold shows ephemeral-storage at 97%. Node pool uses smaller root volumes to save $$.
Jen: That's a topology + sizing mismatch. Preemptible nodes are cheaper but we probably network-pulled large model cache on startup which temporarily spikes disk. Two failure modes: 1) CA adds nodes too small for image cache, 2) HPA reacts before nodes are fully ready and pods land on tainted nodes then get evicted.
Liam: Can we adjust HPA to use a slightly delayed metric or scale-up limit? HPA has stabilizationWindowSeconds and behavior.policy. Maybe add stabilization of 30-60s to avoid overshoot.
Priya: Also VPA is set to auto-apply recommendations for some non-GPU workloads; are we mixing VPA on these pods? VPA might change resources causing restart + image refresh.
Sam: VPA is annotation'ed off for the batch inference pods, but some sibling pods in the same Deploy cause node pressure during rollout.
Marco: Suggest two-prong: 1) change nodepool to use larger boot disks or a local cache disk for models (gcePersistentDisk or AWS EBS) for warm nodes; 2) adjust CA scaling policy and mark preemptible pool as "warm" with min-nodes and surge capacity so CA doesn't spin up tiny nodes repeatedly.
Jen: Agreed. Also set HPA.behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds=45 and increase .policies to limit 3 pods/30s so we don't request a huge burst. Add a cooldown annotation to the external-metrics-adapter so transient spikes don't trigger immediate spikes.
Sam: I'll test HPA changes. Quick question: can we make the HPA read aggregated queue depth across pods differently? Right now it's per-pod external metric which tends to amplify.
Priya: Yes — external metric type "AverageValue" vs "Value" matters. If you're using pods/external metric type Value it multiplies. Change to per-pod average or use object metric arithmetic to scale by total backlog / desired_batch_size.
Liam: We should also set podPriority for these jobs so CA doesn't preempt them when nodes are tight. Use a PriorityClass "inference-batch-critical" with high priority so eviction order favors other pods.
Marco: And add node taints + pod tolerations for preemptible pool; prevent non-batch traffic from landing there. That reduces noisy neighbors pulling images.
Sam: Good call. I'll spin up a small repro with simulated backlog and try: HPA behavior changes, AverageValue metric, podPriority, and bump boot disk size on a staging preemptible pool.
ops-bot: Deployment event: created horizontalpodautoscaler/inference-batch-hpa (by Sam)
Jen: Keep an eye on CA scale events in the 10-15m window. If CA still flaps, we may need to add a node provisioning grace window in our autoscaler config (gke: node-provisioning-grace; k8s CA: expander/scaleDownDelay).
Sam: Will report results. If this fixes, we can roll to eu-west and then other regions. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Priya: If you need infra support ping me, I can create a temp larger-disk nodepool and test warm cache.
Sam: Pinged. Assigning to me and Priya to run the test and follow up in this thread.
